intervention at page 7: The Agency is described as an autonomous, independent state body supervising the lawfulness of personal data processing.
intervention at page 7: The Agency is led by a director elected by the Assembly for five years, renewable once, with a deputy.
recommendation at page 10: The Commission report, as relayed, stresses urgent, full GDPR alignment and adoption of legislation aligned with the Law Enforcement Directive.
recommendation at page 10: EU recommendations, as relayed, point to reforms ensuring the Agency's autonomy in engaging staff and managing its budget.
recommendation at page 10: The Agency's staff numbers and budget funds urgently need increasing so that it can perform its tasks and powers effectively.
barrier at page 10: Low salaries and insufficient financial support limit the Agency's work and its ability to monitor data protection effectively.
recommendation at page 10: The Agency needs greater coordination and systematic consultation on all sectoral laws and legislative initiatives.
recommendation at page 10: Follow-up of the Agency's recommendations and regular communication with the Assembly should improve to reach high data protection standards.
finding at page 10: The Agency calls delivering these urgent reform priorities key to speeding European integration and alignment with EU legislation.
intervention at page 10: In April 2022 the Agency prepared a draft law amending the data protection law to ensure the Agency's full autonomy and independence.
barrier at page 10: The existing law contains no solutions giving the Agency all the resources it needs to perform its tasks and powers.
intervention at page 10: The amendments would let the Agency manage its financial and human resources independently, without influence from other institutions.
barrier at page 10: Budget constraints and reduced staff currently hinder the Agency's functioning and performance of its statutory tasks.
intervention at page 10: A draft law transposing the Law Enforcement Directive went to the Assembly, but the Government withdrew it in September 2022 during second reading.
intervention at page 16: The Agency adopted a Decision establishing a Methodology for harmonising sectoral legislation with the data protection law.
metric at page 19: 206 of the representations submitted in 2024 were submitted electronically.
intervention at page 20: The Agency's website offers an e-classroom tool with data protection resources for citizens and bodies processing personal data.
intervention at page 29: The Agency has observer status at the European Data Protection Board.
intervention at page 25: The Agency keeps encouraging electronic submission of requests and documents and implementing new technologies in supervisions.
finding at page 25: In 2024 most requests on data protection violations and for supervisions were submitted through the Agency's web platform.
intervention at page 25: GIZ and the Agency began three data protection videos in 2024 under a Western Balkans digital instruments project on digital literacy and online security.
intervention at page 25: An e-classroom web tool from an EU-supported project by Metamorphosis and Konekt is available on the Agency's website.
intervention at page 25: In 2024 the Agency took over the e-classroom website and began using it as a platform for data protection e-training.
metric at page 26: More than 50 people completed the e-classroom's data protection quizzes.
intervention at page 27: The Agency joined the inter-ministerial working group preparing the National Cybersecurity Strategy, attending 4 meetings in 2024.
intervention at page 27: The Agency signed 2 memoranda of cooperation with institutions in 2024.
intervention at page 30: Strategic goal 3 covers data protection culture: cooperation with supervisory bodies and sectors, training, and greater Agency transparency and visibility.
intervention at page 31: Strategic goal 4 activities cover accountability tools, certification and codes of conduct, and networking and position of data protection officers.
intervention at page 31: Progress on the Strategy will be monitored through defined key indicators linked to its goals and activities.
intervention at page 31: The Agency will create mechanisms with the Justice and Public Administration ministries and others to monitor the Strategy's progress.
intervention at page 31: The Agency adopted a new Rulebook on security of personal data processing on 26 December 2024.
intervention at page 31: The Agency also adopted rulebooks changing the rules on notifying personal data breaches and on carrying out supervision.
intervention at page 31: The rulebooks were developed through an EU Twinning project on the modernised data protection framework by German and Croatian experts.
intervention at page 31: The Rulebook applies from 1 July 2025, and controllers and processors must align with it within six months.
finding at page 34: The Agency says it achieved significant progress in applying the legal framework despite difficult regulatory and financial circumstances.
recommendation at page 34: The Agency will have to submit an initiative with proposed amendments to the data protection law.
recommendation at page 34: The Agency will have to submit an initiative with proposed amendments to the Law on Misdemeanours.
recommendation at page 34: The Agency will have to promote the need for a law transposing the Law Enforcement Directive.
recommendation at page 34: The Agency will have to promote the need to implement the Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI.
recommendation at page 34: The Agency will have to seek sufficient funds for its tasks and independence in spending them.
recommendation at page 34: The Agency will have to adjust its institutional capacities to the systematisation and to its tasks and powers.
recommendation at page 34: The Agency will have to give opinions on laws and by-laws to align them with the data protection law.
recommendation at page 34: The Agency will have to initiate amendments to laws and by-laws to align them with the data protection law.
recommendation at page 34: The Agency will have to give controllers and processors guidance, warnings and orders to align processing with data protection rules.
recommendation at page 34: The Agency will have to give opinions on consultation requests where impact assessments show high risk without mitigating measures.
recommendation at page 34: The Agency will have to give opinions on proposed international agreements and instruments on data protection.
recommendation at page 34: The Agency will have to carry out activities improving its public perception and visibility.
recommendation at page 34: The Agency will have to increase the number of trainings for its staff.
recommendation at page 34: The Agency will have to start preparing a Communication Strategy 2026-2030.
recommendation at page 34: The Agency will have to promote its Methodology so that ministries assess data protection impact when drafting laws.
recommendation at page 34: The Agency will have to strengthen the position of data protection officers within controllers.
